canonical_title: White House launches Super Intelligence Force led by Jay Clayton
organizations: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
treatment: Repeat only for the 120-day report, binding policy or enforcement changes, material incident-reporting requirements, or a significant membership/mandate change.
known_facts: President Donald Trump announced the Super Intelligence Force on October 4, 2026 to coordinate federal AI policy and U.S. leadership efforts.
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton leads the task force; reported members include FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson, Pentagon CTO Emil Michael and OPM Director Scott Kupor.
The task force is expected to report on AI risks, opportunities and the federal oversight role within 120 days, including review of security-incident reporting and existing authorities.
reinclude_only_if: The task force publishes its 120-day report or concrete recommendations.
A binding rule, executive action, enforcement mechanism or incident-reporting requirement is adopted.
The mandate or membership changes materially.
notes: Night-window hard delta: formal launch and named leadership became public on Oct. 4; distinct from the previously covered voluntary White House AI safety accord.
